skill.name: cooper-manage-inboxes
skill.description: Manage Cooper Email inboxes through a connected MCP server. Create temporary or custom-domain addresses, inspect settings, pause delivery, and delete inboxes with explicit confirmation.
skill.summary: Manage Cooper Email inbox lifecycles with scoped access, temporary addresses, and deletion safeguards.
skill.author: cooper-email

content.value_statement: Managing temporary addresses and inbox settings can create duplicate inboxes or accidental data loss. This skill guides Cooper MCP operations with retry identifiers and explicit deletion confirmation.
actual_capabilities: Identify the connected account, inspect key scope, list inboxes, and check plan limits.
Check username availability and create inboxes with stable retry identifiers.
Create batches of temporary inboxes with labels and expiration settings.
Create custom-domain inboxes after checking ownership, verification, and receiving status.
Update display names, metadata, screening, send mode, and paused or active status.
Delete inboxes or conversations after identifying the target and obtaining explicit confirmation.
limitations: Requires a connected Cooper MCP server and permissions for the requested operations.
Does not cover sending email, reading messages, triage, or MCP setup.
Custom domains require account eligibility, DNS publication, and successful verification.
Temporary inbox cleanup occurs through a daily cron, not necessarily at the exact expiration time.

use_cases.title: Provision temporary test inboxes
use_cases.description: Create labeled inbox batches with expiration settings for isolated test runs.

use_cases.title: Maintain team inbox settings
use_cases.description: Inspect inbox status, update display names, and pause unused inboxes without deleting their messages.

use_cases.title: Prepare custom-domain addresses
use_cases.description: Check domain readiness and account limits before creating project inboxes on a verified domain.

prompt_templates.title: List current inboxes
prompt_templates.prompt: List my Cooper Email inboxes and show their addresses and statuses. Do not change anything.

prompt_templates.title: Pause a selected inbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Cooper inbox at [address] and pause it. Preserve its messages and report its resulting status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: make a reversible lifecycle change.

prompt_templates.title: Create temporary inboxes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [count] temporary Cooper inboxes with prefix [prefix], label [label], and a [hours]-hour lifetime. Check plan limits first.

prompt_templates.title: Provision a custom-domain inbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that [domain] belongs to my account and receives mail. Create [username] using stable client_id [identifier]. Stop if verification or permissions fail.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: combine domain checks and retry-safe creation.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: pause a selected inbox while preserving its messages.
output_examples.output: Inbox status: paused. Existing messages retained. Sending and new incoming mail are stopped.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: delete a selected inbox before confirmation has been given.
output: Deletion pending confirmation for inbox [inbox id] at [address].
Deleting this inbox also deletes its messages.
Confirm this exact target before deletion proceeds.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: create an inbox on a domain that is not verified.
output_examples.output: No inbox created. The domain must be verified and enabled for receiving mail before creation can proceed.

best_practices: Check the connected account, permission scope, and plan limits before creating resources.
Use stable client identifiers for retries and verify domain ownership before custom-domain creation.
Confirm exact deletion targets, offer pausing when appropriate, and keep API keys outside chat and logs.
anti_patterns: Treating a request to stop mail as permission to delete an inbox and its messages.
Reusing deletion confirmation after the target changes or broadening an inbox-scoped key.
Inventing domain verification status or exposing API keys and unrelated mail.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a connected Cooper MCP server. The available account and key permissions determine which operations can succeed.

faq.question: Can this skill send or read email?
faq.answer: No. Sending uses cooper-send-email, while reading and triage use cooper-check-email.

faq.question: Can I create temporary inboxes in batches?
faq.answer: Yes. Batch creation supports a count, optional prefix and labels, and expiration settings. Expired inboxes are deleted by a daily cron.

faq.question: What is required for custom-domain inboxes?
faq.answer: The domain must belong to your account, be verified, and have receiving enabled. Adding domains requires an eligible plan.

faq.question: What happens when I pause an inbox?
faq.answer: Pausing stops sending and new mail without deleting existing data. Setting the status to active resumes operation.

faq.question: How does deletion confirmation work?
faq.answer: The exact inbox id and address require explicit confirmation. Approval-mode deletion also requires a verified owner to confirm an emailed link.
